Irish Coast Guard: its releases are Department of Transport press releases on gov.ie; no RSS or Atom address for gov.ie press releases was found by search. MerrionStreet.ie (the government news service) has a feed, but a relay service shows its last posts in January 2024; not opened.
Not tested from GitHub's runner with the watch's user agent: every feed above was opened with the fetch tool, a different client. The RNLI 403 shows a site can treat the two differently.
notes: Three of the ten services have a feed that returned items on 23 Nov 2026: KNRM (two national feeds), the Canadian Coast Guard and Maritime New Zealand. That is fewer than five, so status partial. Before enabling any of them, three things matter for the watch. (1) Language: watch/keywords.json is English-only, so KNRM's Dutch items would almost never match. Reddingrapporten is an incident log, one call-out per item, so it may be better served by a per-source rule that labels every item 'rescue' than by keywords. Candidate Dutch patterns for a person to check: redding, verdronken, vermist, zoekactie, omgeslagen. (2) Dates: KNRM's news feed carries one pubDate in September 2027. The watch sorts by published, so that item would sit at the top of feed.json until then; clamping dates later than first_seen would prevent it. Maritime NZ's items have no pubDate at all, so the watch would record published as null and sort them by first_seen. (3) Freshness: Maritime NZ's newest item is from 25 June 2026; the feed may have stopped updating, and a person should compare it with the news page before relying on it. No feed above states terms of use. Kinds: KNRM Reddingrapporten = incident log; KNRM Nieuws = organisation news with some rescues; Canadian Coast Guard = press releases and advisories (national); Maritime NZ = press releases (national regulator, includes rescue coordination news).
